account: It is day 1 at 07:00. I am in the town hall office with the secretary nearby, having read and returned the appointment books. Today’s business is office work at eight, a grain inspection at the east-bank mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage at fifteen, office again at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen. The notable addition is an eighteen hundred meeting with the neighbour at town hall. The neighbour requested it during yesterday’s tea, I accepted, and the secretary recorded it in an addendum. It was described as an ordinary meeting or little chat; its subject and any preparation requirements remain unknown to me. I have no evidence that it concerns anything unusual. Yesterday the secretary reported no incoming correspondence, bills, or waiting visitors. The town accounts record contains my report of 128 emeralds in the treasury, unchanged, but no separate account papers were supplied. I asked the secretary to notify me of grain reports or council letters. I have not yet received any such report. I should keep today’s appointments and learn what the neighbour wishes to discuss rather than assume a purpose.
